choice: add checked_boot, the boot id of checked_at, written by both beat and checked; the earlier-boot filter in _latest_checks keeps a row by checked_boot, falling back to seen_boot for rows written before the column existed
why: a row carries two stamps, last_seen and checked_at, so it needs a boot for each. The round-4 clearing left a failed check with no boot after a reboot, and the filter kept it. Once the wall clock rolled back on a later boot, its larger checked_at masked a fresh current-boot success. This replaces the round-4 note that one boot stamp per row was enough

decision: row with no boot after a current-boot success
choice: once this boot has a success, the earlier-boot filter keeps rows whose check boot (checked_boot, else seen_boot) is this boot and drops rows whose check boot is another boot; a row with no boot at all is dropped only when some row in the group has checked_boot equal to this boot, and kept otherwise
why: this replaces a rule that dropped every row with no boot on the claim that such a row is older than the success. A counterexample disproved it: the previous release beats pid 101 on boot B, restarts, and its pid 202 records a failed check on boot B one second later with no boot stamps; a reader-only upgrade then reported pid 101 up where main reported pid 202 stale. Every current writer, beat and checked alike, stamps checked_boot, so only a current-release check on this boot proves a row with no boot was written before it; that still drops the earlier-boot failure whose larger checked_at, after a wall-clock rollback, masked a fresh success. Without such a check a row with no boot may be from this boot and is kept, as on main. When only old-release writers wrote the rows, the data cannot tell an earlier-boot row from a current-boot one, the same limit main has. If an old-release process keeps writing alongside a new one, its later failed check with no boot is dropped once the new one has checked on this boot. A backfill at migration was rejected: an old-release process still running after the migration writes the same NULL rows
